title: Collaborative voice and code coordinator
learning_objectives: Propose and revise an inspectable architecture
problem_statement: Design a coordinator that accepts voice/text turns, streams updates and sends untrusted Python to a separate isolated execution worker.

clarification_facts.retry_behavior: Browser may retry after response loss

progressive_constraints.title: Separate trust boundaries
progressive_constraints.description: Connect client, coordinator and execution worker without placing arbitrary code in the API process.

progressive_constraints.title: Lost response
progressive_constraints.description: A browser retries a request whose execution may already have committed. Name a durable request identity and response replay boundary.

progressive_constraints.title: Cancellation and streaming
progressive_constraints.description: A learner edits code or interrupts speech while work is in flight. State revision fencing and cancellation semantics.

progressive_constraints.title: Twelve app instances
progressive_constraints.description: At 20000 active sessions across twelve app instances, state where cross-node events and mutation authority live.

valid_architecture_families.name: Partition-owned coordinator
valid_architecture_families.description: Sticky session ownership plus durable state and a cross-node event backplane.

valid_architecture_families.name: Stateless API with durable streams
valid_architecture_families.description: Database CAS and durable event streams coordinate independent API instances and worker queues.

common_misconceptions: Retrying a POST is not exactly-once execution.
Cancelling a client promise does not prove a provider or worker stopped.
An in-memory lock in one API instance is not a global lock.

hint_ladder.level_1: Trace a response lost after the worker result commits.
hint_ladder.level_2: Compare partition ownership with a database CAS boundary.
hint_ladder.level_3: Record the request identity and durable result atomically. Fence late events by session epoch and artifact revision. A worker must still satisfy independently accepted isolation; the diagram does not prove gVisor is running.

consolidation: Keep execution isolation, mutation identity, state persistence and streaming replay distinct. A proposed topology cannot certify sandbox behavior or latency.
fresh_transfer_question: How would you recover after an API instance dies while a sandbox job is finishing?
coach_instructions: One clear question at a time. Inspect actual graph and stated assumptions. Do not grade prose by keywords or require a vendor name. Numeric assumptions are learner declarations, not measured performance. Explain when asked, require teach-back, and preserve alternative valid designs. Do not silently edit the diagram.
